solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

S030-01.notes: No rule existed and meetings never mention prices, yet prices stayed close for decades: an unspoken (tacit) understanding. 'formal' contradicts 'no rule'/'never mention'; 'fragile' contradicts decades of stability; 'contentious' unsupported. Difficulty comes mainly from knowing 'tacit'.

S030-02.notes: Small size vs. major significance: the size gave a false impression of the significance (belied). 'reflected' and 'determined' state the opposite relationship; 'exaggerated' makes no sense with 'modest'. Vocabulary ('belied') is the hurdle; 'reflected' is an attractive trap for students who don't know the word.

flags: minor: D paraphrases the text's central claim ('no individual completes the return') almost directly, so it is close to a lookup.
S030-03.notes: Text's point is that the annual migration cycle spans several generations. A is a detail; B and C unsupported. Facts check out: overwintering monarchs die en route north and later generations reach Canada, with fall migrants typically 3-4 generations removed.

S030-04.notes: Plentiful/easy-to-get food is still low in protein, so content matters more than ease of access. A reverses the effort claim; C speculative; D contradicts (too little protein). Consistent with Murray et al. 2015 (Edmonton coyotes, human food linked to poorer condition and mange).

flags: minor: D is the only choice expressing changes as proportions, which matches the conclusion's 'relative to each building group's starting level' and makes it easy to spot.
S030-05.notes: Verified: dot film 20->6 = 14/20 = 70%; UV glass 40->22 = 18/40 = 45%; netting 10->4 = 6/10 = 60%. D accurate and supports the claim. A is true (18 is the largest absolute drop) but undercuts the claim; B and C are true but irrelevant to relative effectiveness. A is the main trap.

S030-06.notes: Text 2 says experience with people shapes the skill more than recognized, which challenges an 'inborn, from domestication' account. A misreads the wolf evidence; B is about chimpanzees, which Text 2 does not address; D unsupported (shelter dogs struggle). Consistent with Hare et al. and Udell et al. (2008) findings.

flags: minor: A is the only choice that mentions the result at all; B, C and D are clearly off-goal, so the item is easy to eliminate.
S030-07.notes: Surprise = more receptor types (12 vs 3, exactly four times) yet worse discrimination. Math checks (12/3 = 4). Matches Thoen et al. 2014 (Science).

S030-08.notes: First sentence gives an ecological benefit; second gives a drawback (conflict with fishers): a contrast, so 'Even so'. 'As a result' is a mild trap (the appetite does cause the conflict, but it does not follow from kelp regrowth); 'Similarly' and 'In other words' clearly wrong.

S030-09.notes: The appositive 'a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown script' opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb 'has resisted'. A leaves the appositive unclosed; B mismatches the punctuation (comma open, dash close); D splits the subject from its verb. Facts OK (vellum carbon-dated to the early 1400s; 20th-century codebreakers such as Friedman tried and failed).

S030-10.notes: The 'that' clause needs a finite verb; the killing happened before he noticed it (past), so past perfect 'had killed'. 'has killed' is the wrong tense for a past narrative; 'killing' and 'to kill' leave the clause without a finite verb. Facts OK (Fleming returned in early Sept 1928; Penicillium lysed the staphylococci near it).

S030-11.notes: The Draupner measurement (about 26 m amid about 12 m seas) was hard instrumental evidence that conflicted with models predicting such waves would be extremely rare. A is wrong because the measurement was not exaggerated and the models did not explain it; B is wrong because the revision comes in sentence 3; C is a trap that distorts 'more common than once believed' into 'more common today'. Facts check out (Draupner, 1 Jan 1995, about 25.6 m maximum height, about 12 m significant wave height).
